children.name: Eupetes
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Malaysian Rail-babbler, one of the most enigmatic passerines in Southeast Asia. It has an exceptionally long neck, long legs, and a strikingly long tail, giving it a superficial resemblance to a rail. It is a skulking, ground-dwelling bird of the remote lowland forest floor, with a distinctive, far-carrying call that is far more frequently heard than the bird is seen.

children.name: Eupetes macrocerus
children.description: The rail-babbler or Malaysian rail-babbler (Eupetes macrocerus) is a brown and pied rail-like ground-living bird. It is the only species in the genus Eupetes and family Eupetidae. It lives on the floor of primary forests in the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra (the nominate subspecies macrocerus), as well as Borneo (ssp. Borneensis). It is distantly related to African rockfowl. Its population has greatly decreased because much of the lowland primary forest has been cut, and secondary forests usually have too dense a bottom vegetation or do not offer enough shade to be favourable for the species. However, it is locally still common in logged forest or on hill-forest on slopes, and probably not in immediate danger of extinction. The species is poorly known and rarely seen, in no small part due to its shyness.
